newsitem.title: CANADA: Barshefsky, Sato meet to discuss trade issues.
newsitem.headline: Barshefsky, Sato meet to discuss trade issues.

text.p: U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and Japanese Trade Minister Shinji Sato met Thursday to discuss pressing trade issues between the two countries including efforts by Japan to deregulate its economy.
At the start of the meeting Sato told Barshefsky that Japan would carry out plans to deregulate its economy to lower costs to consumers.

The United States is anxious for Tokyo to reduce some of the regulations it says creates barriers to imports. Barshefsky and U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin have said they do not want Japan to export its way out of recession and that they do not expect to see a big increase in the U.S. trade deficit with Japan.

Barshefsky and Sato are in Toronto for a meeting of the Quadrilateral group or "Quad" -- the trade ministers from the United States, Japan, European Union and Canada. The ministers are expected to discuss a wide range of issues including negotiations under the World Trade Organization (WTO) on opening financial services markets.

The ministers hope to build on the momentum of last year's successful negotiations to lower tariffs on information technologies and on an agreement earlier this year to open telecommunications markets around the globe to more outside competition.
They are also expected to discuss China's bid to enter the WTO.
